content:
I can't edit my message on the Zulip Web app. On the Android app, I get this error:

Message not saved

The server said: 'prev_content_sha256' value does not match the expected value.
And refreshing didn't help? (or on Android, force-quitting the app)
I restarted my phone, but it didn't help.

That's a check that is supposed to protect against concurrent modification of the message.

Can you link to the message in question?
Here's the link to my message: #maths > accessibility and descending chains @ 💬.

I've had this problem before, solved it by going to the browser and logging into zulip and editing the message on the browser, then when I come back to the app it updates the message on the app and I can edit the message on the app again

Hm -- I see some edit history on that message:

Are you not able to make more edits, or were those the edits you were trying to make?
I want to make more edits, but I can't.
OK, interesting. Let me poke.

I got this now on the web app.
I edited this message before, and when I checked back later the edit seems have been reverted, and now any attempt to edit says Error editing message: Message was edited by another client..

Any updates? Can you tell what's going on with that message?

Hm, thanks for the reminder.

I dug into this, and I think this is a case of a race condition with a cache fill, which is (a) causing you to still see the old version, and (b) since your client only knows about that old version, its attempts to edit it again get told "you're out of date" (not incorrectly).

For instance, I don't see your "Edit: hmm maybe not" in that message in the UI, but the database has it.

I don't see any inconsistency with the previously-reported message, but that's not surprising, since it's longer ago and is more likely to have fallen out of cache and gotten re-filled with the actual database value.

Interesting that both recent reports have been in this same Zulip instance. I don't have a theory for that.
It looks like there's no edit time threshold configured for this instance, so -- @Bulhwi Cha, does it work if you try to edit your message now?

Alex Vandiver said:

(b) since your client only knows about that old version, its attempts to edit it again get told "you're out of date" (not incorrectly).

This happened in the same client that I edited on, so it definitely was aware of the new version at some point.
The only time I switched clients was after I got the error and before I reported it here, to check if switching clients helps.

Alex Vandiver said:

I dug into this, and I think this is a case of a race condition with a cache fill, which is (a) causing you to still see the old version, and (b) since your client only knows about that old version, its attempts to edit it again get told "you're out of date" (not incorrectly).

This makes sense to me but then since it knows it's out of date why isn't it fetching the latest version of the message

Yes, the sending client certainly was aware of it when it sent it. The cache in question is the server-side one which all clients (regardless of if they sent the information) are fed information about messages from. We use a cache there because "give me the messages in the channel" is a very common codepath, and one which needs to be fast. The "is this hash of the contents up to date" check (which happens server-side during edits) does not use that cache.

The fix is to chase down where the race condition is which is causing the cache to get filled with the out-of-date data. This is a common flavor of problem when you have a transaction-aware system (i.e., a relational database with transactions) which is being fronted by a non-transactional cache (in this case, memcached).
Is recomputing the cache every 24h feasible? At least for topics that had some activity in that time?
I'm not clear why that would ever be preferable to just not having the bad content in the cache in the first place?
Since it sounded like it's hard to find this race condition, so a temporary fix would be nice

We've identified the exact race condition, and we'll have a fix out in not too long.

If you're just concerned about that message, I've flushed it from the cache, and reloading will now show its real value and thus allow edits.

Alex Vandiver said:

It looks like there's no edit time threshold configured for this instance, so -- Bulhwi Cha, does it work if you try to edit your message now?

Yes! In fact, the message had already been fixed before I looked at it again.

Alex Vandiver said:

We've identified the exact race condition, and we'll have a fix out in not too long.

Is the fix already deployed? This just happened again; can't edit this message, I never swapped clients.
(idk if you're still here or moved to Anthropic already)
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/39249 is the fix, which has not yet been deployed.
Sorry for the delay -- the last month has been ... busy.
I've poked it harder into some review queues.
